title: prefill-decode: chunked speculative prefill + stage-overlap + kernel scheduler optimizations
author: Priya Nambiar
description: Motivation: reduce end-to-end latency and GPU idle time for mixed prefill/decode workloads by improving overlap between prefill and decode stages, introducing chunked speculative prefill to reduce wasted work on early-stopping sequences, and adding a kernel-aware scheduler that places prefill and decode kernels to maximize occupancy. Changes: 1) Chunked speculative prefill: break large prefill requests into configurable chunks that can be speculatively decoded in parallel with remaining prefill chunks. This reduces tail latency when users request long context windows and early-termination of decode can salvage work. 2) Stage overlap orchestration: introduce a lightweight stage orchestrator in the pipeline runtime to allow prefill, kv-cache population, and decode micro-batches to overlap when dependencies allow. The orchestrator enforces correctness with explicit readiness markers and KV cache versions. 3) Kernel scheduler heuristics: implement a kernel selection/scheduling layer that prefers co-locating kernels with complementary memory/compute patterns, prioritizes low-latency kernels for small decode steps, and throttles speculative prefill pressure under high throughput. 4) KV cache optimizations: add async prefetch/writeback for chunked prefill boundaries to reduce stalls when decode reads recently-populated cache entries. 5) Continuous batching adjustments: update batching windows to account for chunk boundaries and speculative rewards, enabling more aggressive micro-batching without violating latency SLOs. Testing and results: microbenchmarks show median tail latency reduction of 18-28% across our internal chat workloads with end-to-end token throughput improving by ~12% on A100 nodes. Memory overhead stays within 5% due to chunked memory reuse. Backwards compatibility: new defaults are conservative and can be toggled via runtime flags. Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag redwood.prefill_speculative_chunking and staged rollout via Dedicated clusters for 2 weeks before full host rollout. See linked Linear tasks for rollout plan.

conversation: Ethan: The chunking approach looks promising but I'm concerned about correctness when speculative decode finishes earlier than remaining prefill chunks. Priya: We track per-request KV cache versions and the orchestrator exposes a readiness marker; decode will only consume KV entries up to the last fully-written version and speculative decode is allowed to continue using its own provisional cache until commit. Marisol: Can we avoid nightly OOMs when users submit many long prefill requests? Priya: Added chunked memory reuse and backpressure in the batcher; when memory pressure is high we increase chunk granularity and fall back to non-speculative prefill. Jacob: Please add a perf regression test for short-context workloads to ensure no regressions. Priya: Added tests in tests/perf and ran against internal perf lab. CI initially failed lint on a header include, fixed in follow-up commit. Post-merge note from SRE: monitor p99 decode latency for the first 48h after rollout.
release_notes: Optimizations for prefill/decode pipeline: chunked speculative prefill reduces tail latency and GPU idle time, stage-overlap orchestration enables safe concurrency between prefill and decode, kernel scheduler improves placement for mixed workloads. Feature behind runtime flag redwood.prefill_speculative_chunking.
